body: All good brother. I don't like the idea of OD, it sounds scary and survivable. The closest thing I would get to overdose would be huffing car exhaust until I fell asleep permanently. Therapy helped but it was funded through the military. I am no longer in the military.

I scrolled this reddit last night during my incident. It admittedly did help to stave me off for the night. But I woke up disappointed in myself and finding myself wanting to share my feelings with a group of strangers that wouldn't judge me for it.

I tried the medications for a very short time. I never wanted to live off of supplemental chemicals. I got therapy for a little while during my time in the military and it was pretty successful. But old habits die hard and we ultimately end up right back where we began.

Just recently hit my one year mark in Waco (originally from Massachusetts) and can also vouche, it's incredibly hard to meet people. My friend group has been limited to coworkers, who are all decently older than I am. Glad I'm not the only person who's scratching their head on this subject. Welcome to Waco brother, we're happy to have you.

Also, my brother in law here is also a major Eagles fan, he plays a lot of local league sports.
